refresh: Read nightly. The publisher says it updates within two working days of a new sample, with a monthly refresh that may include corrections.

safe_for: Monthly reporting and long-term trends, once the conditions shown are met.
how_to_use: Join on codes, never names. Count below-limit results with a stated method. Mark recent months as part-complete. State whether pollution samples are in.
known_issues: Below-limit results, late streams, default clock times, and one name covering two scales. Times carry no zone marker.

coverage: Every North West point, open and closed
safe_for: Looking up a point's type and status, and place-based reporting, once stand-in locations are set aside.
how_to_use: Join on the point's code. Keep stand-in locations off maps. Labels are withheld wherever they could hold personal or business details.
known_issues: Stand-in coordinates, open points with no recent results, and labels that run several fields together.

source: Environment Agency Bathing Water Quality service
licence: Open Government Licence v3.0, as the service's help pages state.
attribution: Contains Environment Agency information © Environment Agency and/or database right
refresh: Read nightly. Samples are taken in the bathing season only.
coverage: The latest bathing season, across England. Only points that can be linked to North West results are compared.
safe_for: An independent check on the results service. It is used here for reconciliation only.
how_to_use: The only link to the results service is a five-digit code inside a free-text label, so a governed lookup is needed.
known_issues: Some points can't be linked. The comparison covers E. coli at linked points only, and doesn't compare the below or above sign.
